texts.preamble: Attur Taluk Starch And Sago vs Food Safety And Standards Authority Of ... on 6 July, 2018 Author: T.Raja Bench: T.Raja In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 06.07.2018 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice T.Raja W.P. No.16825 of 2018 and W.M.P. No.20015 of 2018 Attur Taluk Starch and Sago Manufacturers Development Welfare Sangam rep. by its President S.Duraisamy, No.150, Kamarajannar Road, Pudupet, Attur, Salem District. .. Petitioner -vs- 1.Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare), Fda Bhavan, Kotla Road, New Delhi-110 002. 2.Commissioner of Food Safety, No.359, Anna Salai, V Floor, Dms Office Building, Dms Campus, Teynampet, Chennai-600 006. 3.Designated Officer, Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, Salem District. 4.Commissioner, Industries and Commerce, No.36, South Canal Bank Road, Mandavelipakkam, Raja Annamalaipuram, Attur Taluk Starch And Sago vs Food Safety And Standards Authority Of ... on 6 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182015328/ 1 Chennai-28. .. texts.facts: This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner praying for issuance of a writ of prohibition prohibiting respondents 2 and 3 herein from issuing any directions, orders or notification in the exercise of their respective power under Sections 30, 32 and 34 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 to introduce a new process in lieu of the existing process or treatment and equipments for the purposes of manufacturing Tapioca Sago and seeking a direction to respondents 1 and 4 herein to consider dispassionately the existing process and equipments used by the members of the petitioner herein for manufacturing Tapioca Sago and instruct respondents 2 and 3 herein to permit the same without yielding to the false and distorted propaganda made against the existing process by the Large Scale Sago manufactures having vested interest to curtail the Tapioca Sago production of Micro, Small and Medium Scale manufacturing Units. 2.The members of the petitioner Association are . All micro and small scale enterprises including the members of the petitioner herein numbering about 300 in the State of Tamil Nadu, used to store required wet starch for home consumption in feeding troughs constructed with boulder stones or lined with granite slabs. Thinned out wet tapioca starch of required quantity is taken from storage tanks/troughs for daily production of Sago using centrifugal pumps operated with 10 H.P. Motors. Thinned out starch is further processed adding prescribed additives and by stirring/agitating the liquid starch operating centrifugal pumps. This process of cleaning impurities from wet Tapioca starch by adding additives and using centrifugal pumps is in vogue in Tapioca Sago manufacturing Industry since the year 1997. On the other hand large scale sago manufacturing industrial units are using imported Decanters, Hydro-cyclones and separators to purify the starch by investing 4 to 7 crores for purchasing said machineries which consumes more electricity. The disparity in the purity and quality between the Tapioca Sago manufactured operating centrifugal motor pumps and sago manufactured through fully automated process using decanters etc. are so glaring and recognised well by the consumers. As a result of this competitive scenario in marketing sago, large scale manufacturers have started spreading false propaganda that cleaning of Tapioca starch operating centrifugal motor pumps give room for adulteration and application of non-permitted additives and therefore such equipment-centrifugal motor pump shall be banned. While the members of the Association are expecting a solution for the issues cropped up due to the interference with manufacturing process by way of improvement notices, the directions issued by the third respondent to dismantle the processing equipments  centrifugal motor pumps has nothing to do with the requirements of satisfying the food standards and hygiene. Therefore, the petitioner is before this Court seeking the above prayer.
texts.arguments: 3.Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that respondents 2 and 3 have exceeded their power and authority provided under Sections 32 and 34 of the FSS Act in unilaterally directing the Micro, Small and Medium Scale Tapioca manufacturer to dismantle centrifugal pumps used for purifying wet tapioca starch by cleaning naturally occurring impurities and the same is untenable. 4.When improvement notice has been issued, the petitioner has not even questioned the correctness of the same.
